description: CMA opened Phase 2 (in-depth) inquiry. One search summary of the CMA case page gives 15 Sep 2022; other sources say only 'September 2022' so verify the exact day.
European Commission opened in-depth (Phase 2) investigation. Date from analyst memory and not confirmed by the search; the 15 May 2023 EC clearance release should state it.
FTC filed administrative complaint and sought to block the deal. Search sources confirm only 'December 2022'; 8 Dec date from memory. Intraday time not verified.
CMA provisional findings: deal could mean higher prices or fewer choices for UK gamers; remedies notice floated prohibition or divestiture. UK publication so before US open.
CMA addendum narrowed scope of concerns (dropped the console-gaming concern). Date 24 Mar 2023 from the CMA admin timetable summary; confirm on the CMA page.
CMA final report blocks the deal over cloud gaming (formal prohibition; coded other because no CMA block type exists). One source says 28 Apr; the 26 Apr report date is better supported.
European Commission cleared the deal with 10-year cloud-streaming licence commitments after Phase 2.
Judge Corley (N.D. Cal.) denied FTC preliminary injunction; Microsoft's outside date was 18 Jul. Time of day not verified.
CMA cleared the restructured deal (cloud rights sold to Ubisoft). Only a single secondary source seen in the search; date medium confidence.

SAMR conditionally approved after AMD offered a commitment plan on 13 Jan 2022: no bundling, no discrimination, supply continuity, interoperability, 6 years. Bloomberg dated the story 27 Jan; time of day not verified.
DOJ sued to block, alleging harm in at least 23 oilfield markets.
Deal terminated Sunday; $3.5B termination fee. First market session after is Mon 2 May.
DOJ (with states) sued to block Aetna-Humana. 21 Jul date from memory; the results only confirm 'July 2016'.
Judge Bates (D.D.C.) blocked the merger.
Aetna and Humana terminated; Aetna paid $1B termination fee.
DOJ (with states) sued to block Anthem-Cigna. 21 Jul date from memory; results only confirm 'July 2016'.
Judge Jackson (D.D.C.) blocked the merger. NPR dates it 8 Feb; Fortune/Bloomberg pieces are dated 9 Feb and one summary gives 9 Feb. After-close timing is from recollection, not verified.
Cigna purported to terminate and sued in Delaware for the $1.85B fee; Anthem disputed the termination.
Bloomberg reported DOJ antitrust staff leaning against the deal. Exact date and time not verified (story 21-22 Apr 2015).
WSJ reported FCC staff recommending a hearing designation order (a formal HDO was not issued before termination). Yahoo timestamp is about 21:30 ET on 22 Apr, so reaction is 23 Apr.
Comcast terminated the deal. Date from memory; the search did not return the termination report (Benton piece titled The Week The Comcast-Time Warner Cable Deal Died supports the week).
Companies terminated after DOJ said it would not continue with the consent decree being negotiated; no termination fee. KLAC 8-K dated 5 Oct 2016.
European Commission cleared with divestitures (optical and photonic software, RTL power analysis).

SAMR conditionally approved (eight conditions per Caixin): honour contracts, keep interoperability, no bundling, divest optical/photonics and power-analysis units; last major hurdle. Caixin dated 15 Jul; Reuters-based reports say 14 Jul.

Fed and OCC approved (OCC conditional on Discover remediation); DOJ told the agencies it saw no basis to block. 18 Apr 2025 was Good Friday so US equity markets were closed; first reaction session is 21 Apr.
FTC proposed consent order barring Scott Sheffield from Exxon board. 2 May date from memory; FTC press release is in the May 2024 archive.
FTC finalized the consent order 3-2 (Ferguson and Holyoak dissenting).
FTC complaint and proposed consent order barring John Hess from Chevron board (3-2).
FTC finalized the order 3-2; the search says only 'January 2025', 17 Jan taken from the Exxon companion order.
FTC voted 3-0 to reopen and set aside the Chevron-Hess order (and the Exxon-Pioneer one); deal had already closed.
Hess/Stabroek arbitration (ICC) ruling reported for Chevron in the same week as the FTC reversal. Exact day not confirmed; treat as week of 14 Jul 2025.
DOJ sued to block HPE-Juniper (N.D. Cal.). Date from memory; search confirms only the later settlement and a July trial date.
HPE and DOJ settlement: divest Instant On WLAN, license Mist AI source code via auction. Saturday release; first session 30 Jun.
Intel terminated for inability to obtain regulatory approvals in time (SAMR never cleared); $353M fee to Tower.
CNBC reported Qualcomm preparing to give up on NXP as SAMR approval stalled. Time of day not verified.
Qualcomm terminated its tender offer after the SAMR deadline passed with no decision; $2B break fee to NXP. SAMR said 27 Jul that remedies were insufficient.
Federal judge (D. Or.) enjoined the merger; a Washington state judge blocked it about an hour later.
Albertsons terminated the merger agreement the day after the rulings (date from memory; search only confirms deal 'likely dead').
Judge Rochon (S.D.N.Y.) granted FTC preliminary injunction; Capri fell about 45%, Tapestry rose about 14%.
Judge Young (D. Mass.) blocked the acquisition (109-page ruling).
Amgen and FTC settled: no bundling of Horizon drugs, prior approval for related acquisitions, 15-year order. FTC suit was filed May 2023.
SAMR approved with conditions (no tying of Fibre Channel/Ethernet adapters to VMware software, interoperability with third-party hardware, confidentiality); expected close 22 Nov.
